reasons: The cited Section 7.2 imposes a disclose-and-match/right-of-first-refusal obligation on Customer before engaging another provider, which restricts our freedom to source elsewhere and therefore falls squarely within the EXCLUSIVITY rule's concern (de facto exclusivity binding Customer), not the permitted Vendor-side exclusivity.

The redline deletes only the offending paragraph, which matches the preferred position ('no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on Customer') and is the minimal edit that reaches it; no Customer-benefiting exclusivity is disturbed.
Deterministic checks confirm the operation applies and that no residual requirements/sole-supplier obligation on Customer remains.

The comment is accurate (correctly characterises the clause as ROFR/de facto exclusivity, correctly notes the conflict with Section 12.3's acknowledgement of no exclusivity or MFC commitment), uses the [Playbook] prefix, first-person plural, concise professional tone, and offers the category-limited 12-month fallback with performance-based automatic exit.
